source.text: ותעלהו עמה כאשר גמלתו בפר משלש ואיפה אחת קמח ונבל יין ותבאהו בית יהוה שלו והנער נער־׃
source.composition: Normalized WLC with one reconstructed short animal phrase; no bread; retained short narrative. Not a complete 4Q51 transcription.
source.vocalization_policy: Retain base interpretation outside the changed phrase; understand the proposed animal as three-year-old. No ancient pointing recovered.

judgments.animal: Age-related animal remains a moderate semantic research preference, not higher confidence from committee agreement.
judgments.exact_short_phrase: Specified test candidate only; historical priority unresolved. HOTTP brackets it. Published 4Q51 instead has [בפר בן ]בקר משלש ולחם, including surviving בקר absent from this proposal.
judgments.bread: Retain base absence for this candidate; omission versus expansion unresolved. Factor 13 is not a demonstrated local conflation.
judgments.narrative: Retain WLC weaning, child-youth and short slaughter/presentation with plural agents. Syriac shows an age/short/no-bread combination, not this exact Hebrew ancestor.
judgments.strongest_countercase: Three bulls is grammatical; the following singular can be collective or refer to one animal. Age could reflect contextual interpretation. Early Hebrew age evidence must still be explained.
judgments.transmission_limit: Redivision plus spelling and grammatical adjustment is a possible multi-step account, not a witnessed sequence. The herd expression could be expansion or older wording; neither direction is proved.

prospective_english.verse24: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with a three-year-old bull, one ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of Yahweh at Shiloh. Now the boy was young.
context_1_22_to_25: But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, “Not until the boy is weaned will I bring him, so that he may appear before Yahweh and stay there forever.”

And Elqanah her husband said to her, “Do what seems good in your eyes. Stay until you have weaned him; only may Yahweh establish his word.” So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with a three-year-old bull, one ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of Yahweh at Shiloh. Now the boy was young.
Then they slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli.
